turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Good morning, thanks for calling Acme Life, you're speaking with Mia. Just so you know, this call is recorded for quality and training purposes. How can I help today?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Hi Mia. I saw your ad online for life cover and filled in the form, but then I thought I'd just ring instead. I wanted to get a rough idea of what it'd cost.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: No worries at all, happy to help. Before we go into any details or pricing, can I please confirm your full name and date of birth?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Sure, it's Sarah Nguyen, and my date of birth is the 14th of March, 1993.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Thanks, Sarah, that matches what came through on the form. So can I ask what's got you thinking about life cover at the moment?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: We've just bought our first place, my partner and I, in Penrith. Settlement was a couple of weeks ago. So now there's this massive mortgage and it suddenly hit me, if something happened to me, he'd be stuck with it.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Congratulations on the new place! That's a really common reason people look at cover. Roughly how much is the mortgage, if you don't mind me asking?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: About four hundred and sixty thousand. We both work full time, but we'd struggle on one income.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Got it. And do you have any kids, or anyone else who relies on your income?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Not yet. Maybe in a few years. It's just us and the dog for now.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Lovely. And do you have any existing life cover, say through your super?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: I think there's something in my super but honestly I've never looked. I assumed it wouldn't be much.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That's pretty typical, the default cover in super is often fairly modest. So for you, with a mortgage of around four sixty, I'd go for $500,000. That clears the loan and leaves a bit of a buffer for your partner. That's what I'd do in your shoes.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Okay. Is that overkill though? I don't want to be paying for more than I need.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: I'd stick with the five hundred. Going lower would leave your partner short on the mortgage, and the difference in price isn't huge. Cover can go anywhere from $50,000 up to a million, but five hundred suits you best.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Right. Do I need a medical or blood tests or anything? I really hate needles.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: No medical exam at all. I just ask you a few health questions and that determines whether we can accept you. Would you like to go through those now?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yeah, go on.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Have you smoked or used any nicotine products in the last twelve months?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No, never.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Have you ever been diagnosed with or treated for cancer, heart disease, stroke or diabetes?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No. I had my appendix out when I was a teenager, that's about it.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That's fine, that doesn't affect anything. And are you currently waiting on any tests or specialist referrals?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: No.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Great, based on that you're eligible. For $500,000 of cover the premium comes to $35 a month.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Thirty-five. Okay, that's less than I expected. Does that stay the same?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Good question. No, the premiums are stepped, so they go up each year as you get older. Thirty-five is what you'd pay this year, and it'll rise gradually from there.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Hmm. And when does it actually start? Like, if I got sick next month, would he get the payout?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Yes, once the policy's in place you're covered from day one, whether it's an illness or an accident. So the mortgage would be looked after straight away.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Okay, that's reassuring. I'm just a bit unsure whether I should talk to my partner first. It's a big thing to sign up to on the spot.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Totally understandable, there's no rush at all. The quote isn't going anywhere, so if you'd rather chat with him and call back, that's completely fine. It's your call.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: What happens if I sign up and then change my mind?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: There's a 30-day cooling-off period. If you cancel within those 30 days, you get a full refund of anything you've paid.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Okay. Honestly, we already talked about getting something when we signed the loan papers, he just left it to me to sort out. I think I'll just do it.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Sure. Before we finalise anything, let me run through it so you're clear. It's Acme Life Cover for $500,000, paid out if you pass away. There's no medical exam, it's based on the health answers you've just given me. The premium is $35 a month to start, and it's stepped, so it goes up each year as you get older. And you've got 30 days to cool off with a full refund. Are you happy to go ahead with that?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yes, I'm happy to go ahead.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Wonderful. I'll take your payment details now, and your policy documents will be emailed to you within the next day. Is the email on your form still the best one?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yep, that's the one.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Perfect. Let's get that set up, and congrats again on the new home, Sarah.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Thanks, Mia. That was easier than I thought.
